params.body:
## What

`<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` in the auth, portal, mobile and error layouts. The share layout already had it.

Portal has no public page: `/` redirects to `/portal`, which redirects to `/login`, and everything else sits behind `portal.auth` or `portal.app`. A stranger only ever sees the login screen, the "sent" screen and error pages. `robots.txt` stays as it is (`Disallow:` empty): a crawler that is blocked never reads the noindex.

## Why

Elixir scores basic tags on what it can reach from outside. Here that was the login screen, so the project carried an SEO task at 50/100 for a page nobody should find. Since abovebeyond-ai/elixir#251, Elixir leaves noindex pages out of the basic-tags score, so this ends the task at the source.

## Tests

`ExampleTest::test_the_login_screen_asks_not_to_be_indexed`. Full suite: 773 of 774 pass. The only failure is `BuildStampTest`, which needs a `.git` directory and fails in a git worktree only; it fails the same way on main in a worktree.
params.title: Mark every page shell noindex: Portal has no page to be found
